model: Regulated utility dividend capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement add-back ($49M; 9M-2026 $39M). Not deducted separately: the capitalised stream is derived from Earnings from Ongoing Operations, which is after SBC expense, so sbc_pct_path is 0 and house and street bases coincide.
inputs.share_count_basis: 752.75M shares outstanding at 2026-10-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) + 1.8M dilutive share-based awards + 1.0M 2023 Exchangeable Notes premium shares (Q3-2026 diluted EPS reconciliation) = 755.5M. Held FLAT: the 27.4M ATM forward shares (physical settlement Dec-2026 to Aug-2027, ~$978M proceeds) and the Feb-2029 Corporate Units purchase contracts ($1.15B) are NOT added, because the stream is per-share guided EPS, which is already net of the plan's equity issuance. Adding them would charge the dilution twice.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC: the capitalised flow is the post-interest dividend. 7.5% = USD risk-free ~4.3% (10-year Treasury) + ~0.65 regulated-utility beta x 5.0% ERP. Same rate in all three scenarios; scenario risk is carried by the driver paths and the weights, not the rate. Compare allowed ROEs of 9.275% (RI) to 9.775% (KY) -- the spread of allowed ROE over cost of equity is why rate base trades above book.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable -- lease liabilities are immaterial (~$10M) and the flow is post-financing.
inputs.nci_treatment: None material in the regulated utilities. Invitium Energy (51% JV with Blackstone Infrastructure) is pre-earnings and carried at zero in base and bear; any contribution in bull is inside the guided EPS upside, attributable basis.
inputs.notes: MODEL: regulated utility valued as a dividend stream capitalised at the cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine. The routing table has no dedicated utility row; owner-FCF is the wrong engine here because reported FCF is structurally negative in a rate-base build (FY2025 OCF 2,629 - capex 4,030 = -1,401; 9M-2026 2,056 - 3,530) and the growth is financed by debt and equity that an unlevered FCF build cannot represent. Per the skill's non-FCF principle the flow the business actually produces for shareholders is the dividend, already after interest, so it is discounted at cost of equity and net debt is NOT subtracted (net_debt held at 0; actual debt $20,890M = ST 679 + current LT 358 + LT 19,853, cash $393M, equity $15,209M at 2026-09-30 are recorded for reference only). ENGINE MAPPING: 'revenue' = ongoing earnings on the current diluted share count (ongoing EPS x 755.5M); growth_rates = ongoing EPS growth; ebitda_margin_path = dividend payout ratio; D&A, capex, tax, SBC and working capital are zero because the stream is already after all of them. So 'FCF' per year = DPS x 755.5M. FY0 is FY2026E, not an actual: base_revenue = $1.94 guidance midpoint (narrowed to $1.92-1.96 on 2026-11-06; 9M-2026 ongoing earnings $1,136M = ~$1.50/share; management 'at least the midpoint') x 755.5M. FY2026 is used as FY0 because the valuation date is six weeks from year end and three of four FY2026 dividends are already paid; Y1 = FY2027. last_fcf = FY2025 common dividends paid ($794M), the stream this model capitalises; the owner-FCF identity (reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income) does not apply on this route. Terminal payout is set to the sustainable level 1 - g/ROE (base 68% at g 3.0%, ROE ~9.5%) so the Gordon value does not capitalise a growth-phase payout. PRICE is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print. History: ongoing EPS $1.60 (FY2023), $1.69 (FY2024, $1,250M), $1.81 (FY2025, $1,344M); DPS $1.03, $1.09, $1.14 annualised (quarterly $0.285 from April 2026). Buybacks: none since FY2021 ($1,003M after the WPD sale); PPL is a net issuer.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management ongoing-EPS guidance (7-9% through 2030), haircut to 7.5% -- not equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.2-2.3%) diverges far more than 30% from GAAP EPS 3yr CAGR (15.9%) and from rate-base growth (~7.7%/yr FY2023-25, $25.0bn to $29.0bn). Book equity is a poor growth anchor here: it was reset by the 2021 WPD sale, the $1.0bn buyback and the 2022 Rhode Island Energy acquisition, and GAAP EPS is distorted by special items (FY2021 loss, FY2022-23 integration costs). Rate base and ongoing EPS are the relevant series.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: reported FCF is negative in every year since FY2021 except FY2021 (capex exceeds OCF by design in a rate-base build), so a CAGR is undefined and SBC adjustment ($49M) does not change the picture. 5yr revenue CAGR is inflated by the May-2022 Rhode Island Energy acquisition; 5yr EPS CAGR is depressed because FY2020 still included the UK (WPD) business. Ongoing EPS 2yr CAGR FY2023-25 is 6.4%; FY2026 guidance midpoint implies +7.2%, FY2027 midpoint +8.2%.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = FY2027 guidance midpoint $2.10 over $1.94. FY2028-30 at 7.5%, below management's 'top half of 7-9%' because all three 2026 rate cases settled below the requested ROE; then a fade to 3.0% as the 2027-30 $25bn plan rolls off.
base.margin_rationale: Payout ratio. FY2027 DPS ~$1.19 (+4.5%, matching the 2026 raise) on $2.10. Payout drifts down to 53% by 2030 as dividends grow slower than EPS to fund capex, then rises to the sustainable 68% (1 - 3.0%/9.5% ROE) as growth fades.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.5%/3.0% = 22.9x terminal dividend, i.e. ~15.6x earnings at a 68% payout; the 25x cap does not bind.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2027 at the top of guidance ($2.12), 9% through 2031-32 as part of the $12-16bn un-planned Kentucky generation is approved and Invitium signs supply agreements; fade to 3.5%.
bull.margin_rationale: Payout falls further (50%) because more capex needs more retained equity, recovering to 65% (1 - 3.5%/10% ROE).
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.5%/3.5% is 25.9x; the 25x dividend cap binds (~16x earnings).

bear.growth_rationale: FY2027 at the bottom of guidance ($2.06), then EPS growth slides to 4-5.5%: data-center load arrives late or not at all, large-load capex is deferred, allowed ROEs keep settling ~100bp+ below ask, and more equity is issued at lower prices.
bear.margin_rationale: Dividend keeps growing ~4-5% so payout rises from 58% to 70% (1 - 2.5%/~8.5% earned ROE).
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% = 20.5x; the 20x dividend cap binds marginally (~14x earnings).

scenario_narratives.base: PPL delivers the FY2027 guidance midpoint and compounds ongoing EPS at 7.5% through 2030 -- inside but not at the top of the raised 7-9% target -- on the $25bn 2027-30 capital plan, with rate base growing roughly 9-10% and the gap to EPS absorbed by the ATM forwards, the 2029 Corporate Units settlement and regulatory lag. Regulators keep granting recovery through DSIC/ISR trackers, FERC formula rates and Kentucky's generation recovery clause, but at ROEs near the 2026 settlements (9.3-9.8%). The LG&E/KU merger closes in January 2027 without material synergy. Invitium contributes nothing. Dividends grow 4-6%, slower than EPS, until growth fades after 2030 and the payout rebuilds to a sustainable 68%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data-center and large-load demand in PJM Pennsylvania and Kentucky converts into signed agreements; the KPSC approves a meaningful part of the $12-16bn of additional Kentucky generation not in the plan, extending 9% EPS growth through 2031-32; Invitium signs hyperscaler energy supply agreements and starts contributing late in the decade; the ISO-NE transmission ROE appeal goes PPL's way. Growth is funded with a lower payout rather than heavier dilution, and the terminal stream is valued at the 25x dividend cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 pattern -- Kentucky 9.775% against 10.95% requested, Rhode Island 9.275% against 10.75% with the second rate year rejected -- hardens into affordability-driven ROE compression as bills rise with the capital plan. Hyperscaler commitments slip or shrink, leaving new Kentucky generation (Mill Creek 6, Brown 12) under-utilised and large-load tariffs contested; coal-fleet environmental rulings add unrecovered cost; Rhode Island stays a drag. Higher rates and a weaker share price make the equity funding more dilutive. EPS growth lands at the low end of FY2027 guidance and decays to 4-5%, then 2.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: earnings depend entirely on regulator decisions and all three 2026 cases settled below ask, while the plan needs continuous equity and debt issuance in a rate-sensitive stock. Base 50%: the FY2027 guidance and the 2027-30 plan are specific and the rate cases are behind it. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right -- hyperscaler contracts that are not signed, KPSC approval of unplanned generation, and an unregulated JV with no contracts.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is a levered claim on rate base earning an allowed ROE; its equity value is the dividend stream that rate-base growth supports, discounted at the cost of equity. The model capitalises per-share dividends built from guided ongoing EPS and an explicit payout path that converges to the payout sustainable at terminal growth. Value is highly sensitive to the cost of equity (a bond-like duration) and to how long 7-9% EPS growth lasts. A 15% hurdle entry price is far below any realistic trading range for a utility: the stock cannot deliver 15% without a rerating, and the required-return table is the more useful read of what today's price implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: +/-1pt on 7.5% moves value by roughly 20-25%; the 10-year Treasury is the dominant external driver
Allowed ROE compression in Kentucky, Pennsylvania and Rhode Island as customer bills rise with the capital plan
Data-center load not materialising: no signed hyperscaler agreements at Invitium, and Kentucky generation built ahead of contracted demand
Equity dilution beyond what guidance embeds (27.4M ATM forward shares, $1.15bn Corporate Units settling February 2029, exchangeable notes)
FY0 is guidance (FY2026E $1.94), not a reported actual; replace with the FY2026 10-K figure in February 2027
Terminal payout and growth: the base terminal multiple of ~15.6x earnings is below the current ~18x forward P/E, so the model assumes multiple compression as growth fades
